claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a dendritic, single-phase BCC microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy reaches approximately 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain and 1273 K.
Introducing oxygen during spark plasma sintering can form TiO precipitates in situ in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
The resulting TiO precipitates can be made fine and uniformly dispersed in TiVNbTa.
Controlled oxygen partial pressure during spark plasma sintering will promote TiO formation.
TiO precipitates impede dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
TiO precipitates stabilize grain boundaries at elevated temperature.
TiO precipitates retard thermally activated dislocation climb and grain-boundary sliding.
Retarding these deformation processes will mitigate high-temperature softening in TiVNbTa.
TiO-containing TiVNbTa will have a yield strength above the approximately 330 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The intervention will moderately improve structural integrity under high-temperature compressive loading.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering produced an NbMoTaWVTi alloy containing a BCC matrix and an FCC TiO precipitate phase.
The reported TiO precipitates in NbMoTaWVTi had an average size of 0.46 micrometers.
The mechanically alloyed and spark-plasma-sintered NbMoTaWVTi alloy was stronger than its as-cast counterpart, with the improvement attributed to grain refinement and precipitation strengthening.
A temperature of 1273 K reflects the thermal environment of a TiVNbTa intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
Compression to approximately 30% strain represents service-relevant mechanical loading for the intermediate layer.
